title: Louisiana Attorney General Opinion 13-0100 (2013-07-10)

July 10, 2013
OPINION 13-0100
61–A–1–LAW-VOTING RIGHTS
La. R.S.17:63 La. R.S. 17:71.5
La. R.S. 17:63 provides that the Iberville Parish School Board must
Honorable Darlene Ourso develop a nine member redistricting plan pursuant to the deadline set
forth in La. R.S. 17:71.3.
Iberville Parish School Board
57030 Ourso Road
White Castle, Louisiana 70788
Dear Ms. Ourso:
Our office has received your opinion request regarding the redistricting of the Iberville
Parish School Board as set forth in La. R.S. 17:63. Specifically, you ask whether the
School Board must comply with provisions of La. R.S. 17:63.
La. R.S. 17:63 states, in pertinent part: “The Iberville Parish School Board shall consist
of nine members. Eight members shall be elected from single-member districts and one
member shall be elected at-large. … No later than the deadline contained in R.S.
17:71.5, the Iberville Parish School Board shall develop a plan to provide for the eight
single-member districts. … Prior to the final adoption of the plan required in this
Subsection, the Iberville Parish School Board shall have a public hearing on the
proposed plan”.
La. R.S. 17:71.5(A) requires school boards reapportion based on the federal census by
December thirty-first of the second year after the census was submitted to the
President.
In conclusion, La. R.S. 17:63 is a validly enacted law and will remain effective unless or
until it is amended or repealed by the legislature or judicially declared unenforceable.
The Iberville Parish School Board should follow the legal requirements set forth in the
statute and create a redistricting plan consistent with the statute. This opinion is
consistent with Shelby County, Alabama v. Holder.1
1 133 S. Ct. 2612 (U.S. 2013).
